acceptance: For 300 seeded random lists of 0 to 6 orders (customers with non-ASCII letters, characters outside the Basic Multilingual Plane, double quotes, commas, backslashes, tabs and newlines, or empty; orders with 0 to 3 lines; every status), `jsonio.write_orders_json(orders, stream)` writes exactly the text that `dump_orders(orders)` returned before the change and returns the number of orders; `dump_orders` returns that same text, for a list as well as for a generator

For 300 seeded random lists of 0 to 6 orders of the same kind, each order with 1 to 3 lines and unit prices up to 100,000.00, `csvio.write_orders_csv(orders, stream)` writes exactly the text that `write_orders(orders)` returned before the change and returns the number of orders; `write_orders` returns that same text, for a list as well as for a generator

The stream can be any object with a `write` method: neither writer calls anything else on it (no `flush`, `getvalue`, `seek`, ...), both pass `write` only `str` values, and neither uses what `write` returns

With no orders, `write_orders_json` writes `[]` followed by a newline and `write_orders_csv` writes the header line `order_id,customer,placed,status,sku,quantity,unit_price` followed by a newline, both return 0, and `dump_orders` and `write_orders` return those texts

For both writers, `orders` can be any iterable, including a one-shot iterator; it is iterated once and never read ahead: when order k+1 is taken from it, the complete text of the first k orders (for JSON everything up to the closing `}` of order k, for CSV every row of the first k orders) has already been written to the stream, and everything written so far is the beginning of the final text (nothing that is not part of it)

For both writers, when the iterable raises, or an element cannot be converted (an element that is not an `Order` raises an `AttributeError` such as `'str' object has no attribute ...`), the exception propagates unchanged, and the text written to the stream is a beginning of the old export of the orders taken before the failure (`dump_orders(...)` or `write_orders(...)` of them) that contains the complete text of each of those orders: neither a separator nor any part of the failing element has been written

`dump_orders(orders)` is `write_orders_json` writing into a string buffer, and `write_orders(orders)` is `write_orders_csv` writing into a string buffer, and each calls its module's streaming writer when it runs: after `monkeypatch.setattr(jsonio, "write_orders_json", replacement)` or `monkeypatch.setattr(csvio, "write_orders_csv", replacement)`, `dump_orders` or `write_orders` returns the concatenation of everything the replacement wrote, and the replacement received the orders

`order_to_dict`, `load_orders` and `read_orders` are unchanged: `load_orders(dump_orders(orders))` gives back equal orders for open orders, with and without lines, `read_orders(write_orders(orders))` gives back equal orders that have lines, and the texts of a small example are exactly as before
